previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and decompensated cirrhosis was admitted for recurrent fever and right upper quadrant pain, similar to prior cholangitis episodes. She spiked fevers up to 102.5 but remained clinically stable without signs of sepsis. Blood cultures were repeatedly negative, imaging showed no biliary obstruction, and inflammatory markers were elevated without a clear infectious source. Antibiotics were withheld, and she became afebrile within 48 hours. The fever of unknown origin may be related to underlying PSC or an immune-mediated process, with an elevated rheumatoid factor prompting rheumatology follow-up. She continued home medications for liver support and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid empiric antibiotics in the future without hepatology consultation.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with PSC complicated by 
___ Class B cirrhosis decompensated with ascites, 
hepatic encephalopathy, and varices who was transferred from 
___ with fevers and hematemesis. Now s/p EGD with 
banding. Patient has remained HD stable without further episodes 
of bleeding. 

# Hematemesis: 
Patient with hematemesis in setting of aggressive vomiting 
concerning for ___ tear versus bleeding of known grade 
II esophageal varices. She underwent EGD demonstrating 2 cords 
of grade II varices that were non-bleeding, but with high-risk 
stigmata (red ___ sign) on one cord. 2 bands were successfully 
placed. Patient remained HD stable with Hg approximately at her 
baseline. She received octreotide x72h, IV PPI, and CFTX for SBP 
ppx. No further hematemesis during her hospitalization. Never 
with any blood per rectum.  She will require carafate 1g QID x 
14 days (last day ___. and repeat EGD in ___ weeks. 

#Fever: 
Febrile to 100.5 on admission. No clear infectious source. CXR 
and urine culture negative with no growth to date on blood 
cultures. In the ICU, the patient was started on treatment doses 
of ceftriaxone, although no tappable ascites pocket was present 
for diagnostic analysis of peritoneal fluid. Given new oxygen 
requirement, some concern that patient may have aspirated during 
EGD. Of note, patient was recently admitted from ___ to ___ with 
fevers and RUQ pain. Antibiotics were not given. She had an 
extensive work up for FUO at that time, notable for elevated 
ESR/CRP, but no precise etiology was determined. Patient 
remained afebrile throughout the rest of her admission and 
received four days of CFTX as ppx for SBP in setting of UGIB. 

#Hypoxemia: 
Patient noted to be intermittently hypoxemic, reportedly worse 
with vasalva. However, no orthodeoxia or platypnea to suggest 
HPS. ECHO bubble study  without evidence of intrapulmonary or 
intracardiac shunt or other concerning cardiac pathology. 
Patient with crackles at bases on lung exam. Thus, hypoxia 
likely due to atelectasis. Her oxygenation improved 
significantly and she was saturated in the high ___ prior to 
discharge without any further episodes of hypoxia. 

# Decompensated Cirrhosis:
___ Class B cirrhosis secondary to PSC decompensated 
with ascites, hepatic encephalopathy, and varices s/p banding on 
___. Continue hydroxyzine, rifaximin, and lactulose. Continued 
home diuretics. 

# Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis:

TID.
